newsitem.title: INDIA: India Apollo Tyres to hike efficiency.
newsitem.headline: India Apollo Tyres to hike efficiency.

text.p: Apollo Tyres Ltd, India's leading tyre maker said in a statement on Tuesday that it was reviewing its work process with a view to enhancing overall efficiency.
"We will be a lean and fighting fit organisation that responds rapidly to market changes," said Onkar Singh Kanwar, vice chairman and managing director.

Apollo declared its results for 1996/97 (April-March) earlier on Tuesday. The company's net profit increased to 363.2 million rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) from 353.1 million in 1995/96. Sales increased to 14.27 billion rupees in 1996/97 from 12.5 billion rupees in the previous year.

The statement said that sluggish markets, severe power cuts and increased input costs did not hold it back from increasing net profit. It added that margins were under pressure due to the high prices of rubber that prevailed through the year.
The statement said that Apollo's sales to the light commercial vehicle sector had grown by 100 percent, and that it was poised to emerge as the largest player in this segment.
Seventy percent of the tyre market is for trucks and buses.
Analysts predict that 1997/98 will be a better year for Apollo, provided there is a recovery in the economy.
"Volumes could increase by 18 per cent at Apollo, if the economy recovers by the second half of 1997/98," said K N Srinivan, auto analyst at Jardine Fleming.
Based on an upturn in the economy by October 1997, analysts expect Apollo's net profit for 1997/98 to rise to an average 500 million rupees, with sales increasing to 15.5 billion rupees.

"Apollo's good years will start in 1998/99, when the results of the economic recovery are reflected in a spurt in demand for tyres," said tyre analyst Sandeep Dhingra at equity research firm S.S. Kantilal Ishwarlal.
